Triage: `pm:queue` + `domain:devx`, type **Bug** — the served `en` bundle and the authored source disagree silently while the gate reports OK; the declared≠enforced shape, as the card itself names it. Lands in `scripts/check-i18n-bundles.mjs` (gate farm → devx). — triage seat Routine.

Triage ruling (PM ruling, premise-bearing — verify the premise first, and report the fork rather than push through if it fails): `en` is a source copy, not a translation, so merge-mode's no-overwrite protection protects the wrong thing there. For `en`, regeneration should track the source (overwrite, or fail red on drift); translated locales (`zh-CN` / `ja-JP` / `es-ES`) keep merge mode exactly as is. **Premise to verify:** nothing hand-edits `en.objects.generated.ts` entries away from source deliberately — if human-authored `en` overrides exist anywhere, the split needs an explicit override channel instead of a blanket overwrite, and that variant comes back to triage.

Scope: first deliverable is the card's own suggested drift scan (every authored `description` vs its `en` bundle `help`) — it sizes the existing gap and doubles as the fix's test fixture; second is the `en`-channel change plus regeneration of whatever the scan finds. If the scan turns up a large pre-existing backlog, report the number before regenerating wholesale.

Size/model suggestion: M, `mode:subagent`, opus.

Verification step A in the report proves this output is byte-identical to what the proposed fix produces, so this listing IS the fix's rewrite set.

## Appendix B — the 5 entries that break triage's premise

All five are `sys_approval_request.fields.status.options.*`. The source is `Field.select([...APPROVAL_STATUSES], ...)` — bare strings — and the extractor seeds a bare-string option from the value itself (`pushEntry(out, [...], opt, 'option', ...)` in `packages/cli/src/utils/i18n-extract.ts`). So the "source text" for these keys is the machine value `pending`, never authored English, and the committed `en` bundle is the only place the English `Pending` exists.

Two corroborating facts, both in-tree:

1. The sibling field `sys_approval_action.fields.action.options.*` in the SAME `en` bundle ships raw lowercase (`submit`, `approve`, `reject`) and shows no drift at all, while its zh-CN counterpart carries real translations. The two fields are already inconsistent in English, and a blanket overwrite spreads the worse half rather than the better one.
2. `fieldOptionLabel` in `@object-ui/i18n` (`packages/i18n/src/useObjectLabel.ts`) resolves the bundle key and falls back to the option's own label, with no humanization anywhere on the path. The regression would reach the screen.

Git history cannot adjudicate hand-edit versus older-source-shape here: this checkout is 147 commits deep and both files were added in the oldest commit. It does not need to — under either origin the effect of a blanket overwrite is identical and user-visible, and no channel currently preserves the text. That is precisely the condition triage attached to its ruling.

## Appendix C — assumptions A / B / C

**A (size) — confirmed, and it is still growing.** 51 entries, 7 files, 6 of 9 packages: non-trivial, not enormous, as expected. The freshest instance is this checkout's own HEAD commit 6b441a842 (#8468 / #8556, landed today): it rewrote `sys_position.name`'s description to "Machine name for the position, unique per organization" and the `clone_position` param helpText to "snake_case machine name, unique per organization", and `check:i18n` went green with the bundle still reading "Unique machine name for the position (e.g. admin, editor, viewer)" — text that is TWO generations stale, because the pre-#8468 source already said "(e.g. sales_manager, hr_specialist)". Successive edits to one field compound into one stale bundle entry, so the count understates the number of lost edits.

**B (en is mechanically identifiable) — confirmed; the fix is a conditional, not a restructure.** `en` is `defaultLocale`, resolved in `commands/i18n/extract.ts` (`--default-locale`, then the config's `i18n.defaultLocale`, then `'en'`), always prepended to the locale list at `i18n-extract.ts:1052-1054`, and ALREADY special-cased at line 1087 where `locale === defaultLocale` takes the seed. The single defect is that the merge branch at line 1080 runs before that special case and wins. The structural work you were worried about is already done in the codebase.

**C (the green gate is part of the defect) — agreed, with one correction.** A gate that regenerates a bundle and then declares success while the bundle disagrees with its source is asserting something false, and that is part of the defect rather than incidental. But overwrite-and-stay-green and red-on-drift are NOT equally available here: both are blocked on the same 5 entries, because under red-on-drift those entries have no non-destructive route to green either — reaching green would still require either the source change (option C) or an override channel (option B). The open choice is therefore source-shaped, not gate-shaped, which is why it goes back to triage rather than being settled in dispatch.

## What I did not do, deliberately

- Did not regenerate any bundle (Zone 1 rule 1: the number is reported before anything is regenerated, and the backlog is entangled with the disputed 5).
- Did not push through the premise fork (Zone 1 rule 3).
- Did not touch `content/docs/releases/`, and did not open a PR — the one-line fix cannot land alone without turning `check:i18n` red on main, so there is no honest partial PR to draft.
- Filed no out-of-scope issues. One candidate exists — bare-string and label-less options go through `pushEntry` (recorded as authored) rather than `pushDerived`, which both erases the `inline` distinction the header documents and makes the coverage gate demand translations of machine identifiers. It is a prerequisite of option B rather than an independent defect, so filing it separately would scatter one decision across two cards. Say the word if you would rather have it on its own card.
